description: Change the shared memory (a tree of folders and .json files; same paths as the memory tool, keep the file extension). Each op also updates the index, so never edit _index.json yourself. add always needs path, value and description (one line shown in the index). To save a new fact: if its folder is not listed yet, make the folder first: {"op":"add","path":"notes/","description":"Notes about people"} ; then {"op":"add","path":"notes/amy.json","value":"Amy likes tea.","description":"Who Amy is"} . Change it: {"op":"set","path":"notes/amy.json","value":"Amy likes coffee."} (description optional). Delete it: {"op":"rm","path":"notes/amy.json"} (a folder that is not empty needs "recursive":true). A key inside a .json object: {"op":"add","path":"notes/people.json#/bob","value":{"likes":"tea"},"description":"Who Bob is"} (make notes/people.json first with value {}). value is plain text or any JSON; do not put JSON inside a string. Keep one text under 2 KB. Errors: NodeExists (use set), NodeMissing (the line says what exists and what to add first), ValueBad, PathBad (writing outside the memory, or the root), ChildrenExist, TargetBad, WriteFailed (read-only for you).

op.description: add = create something new; set = change something that exists; rm = delete

path.description: Like notes/amy.json, notes/amy.json#/phone or notes/trips/ (ends with / = a folder). Relative to the memory root; copy paths as the memory tool prints them.

value.description: add (not for a folder) and set: the content. Plain text is a string like "Amy likes tea."; any other JSON is stored as JSON. For a file that is not .json it must be a string. At most 8000 bytes.

description.description: Required for add: one line saying what this is, shown in the index. Optional for set.

recursive.description: rm: also delete a folder that is not empty.
